newsitem.title: EGYPT: Moslem Brotherhood condemns ruling on Hamas man.
newsitem.headline: Moslem Brotherhood condemns ruling on Hamas man.

text.p: The Moslem Brotherhood of Egypt condemned on Saturday a U.S. federal court ruling in favour of extraditing a Palestinian Hamas militant to Israel.
The brotherhood said in a statement that the the ruling was clearly meant to please American Jews at presidential election time and would add to tension in the Middle East.

In New York on Wednesday a federal judge refused to stop extradition proceedings against Moussa Abu Marzook, head of the political office of the Islamist movement Hamas. Abu Marzook could face trial in Israel on murder charges because of his leadership role in Hamas.

"It is clear that the political dimension in the court's ruling is fundamental, with the aim of winning the approval of Americans Jews in the heat of the competition between the two condidates in the elections," said the brotherhood.

"The Moslem Brotherhood, in condemning this unjust ruling, which harms U.S. policy in the region, assert that it will not help to calm the situation down. On the contrary, it will make it more inflamed and tense. It hopes this ruling will be reviewed in the interests of truth and justice," it added.
The brotherhood is outlawed in Egypt but remains the largest Islamist organisation in the country.
Abu Marzook had asked U.S. District Judge Kimba Wood to determine if he was being wrongfully imprisoned. He argued that another judge had erred in ordering his extradition.
But Wood upheld U.S. District Judge Kevin Duffy's reasoning in issuing the extradition order.
Abu Marzook's extradition will not be immediate because he can appeal against the ruling. In addition, the U.S. Secretary of State has not yet certified the deportation order.
